# BLO-29553: redact credential shapes before `tee` writes the pod log

Change: [BLO-29553](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-29553), AC1(b).

Files: `src/server/pod-log-redactor.ts` (new), `src/server/pod-log-redactor.test.ts` (new), `src/server/job-manifest.ts`, `src/server/job-manifest.test.ts`, `vitest.config.ts`

`claude --output-format stream-json` is piped through `tee <podLogPath>` into the fail-fast awk filter, and **nothing on that leg redacted anything** — the whole adapter package contained zero redaction calls. `podLogPath` is a file on the shared CephFS PVC. The server *does* redact, but only the **derived copy** it tails into `runLogStore` (`heartbeat.ts:4067-4068` `redactSensitiveText`), never the file itself — so a credential the model echoed landed on the PVC in the clear and in **full**, while the store held it redacted. The file is normally unlinked by `cleanupJob`; it survives on the orphan path.

Of the three candidate fixes on the ticket, **(ii) "drop the pod-side file" is void** — that file *is* the pod→server transport (`execute.ts:2338` tails it, `:2352` reads it back for the parse) — and **(iii) "bound the orphan retention window"** is owned and moving on BLO-32734 AC2 / [#2100](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/2100). This is **(i)**, redact at the `tee`, ruled by the CEO on 2026-09-08, following the `failFastFilter` precedent of doing stream work in-pod rather than after the fact.

**The filter sits UPSTREAM of `tee`, deliberately.** Anything downstream scrubs a copy that already landed on the PVC — the same "a batch scrubber must read every credential it redacts" objection that ruled out retroactive scrubbing on this ticket.

**It redacts JSON string values, not the raw line, because the server PARSES this stream.** Raw-text redaction can span JSON structure — `COMMAND_PEM_PRIVATE_KEY_RE` is `[\s\S]*?` — and the failure is not the obvious one: the output stays *valid JSON* while a whole sibling field disappears (measured: `{"a":…,"b":…}` → `{"a":"***REDACTED***"}`). A validity assertion cannot catch that, so the test asserts the key set. Re-serialising a walked value cannot produce either failure. Non-JSON lines take the raw path, which is where byte parity with `redactCommandText` is asserted. The honest limit is asserted rather than hidden: per-value redaction cannot see material split *across* two string values, so a PEM straddling two fields leaves the orphaned footer — a shape that does not occur in a real stream-json event, and strictly better than losing the field.

**The rules are a second copy, and the parity test is what stops it rotting.** The pod has neither the `@paperclipai/adapter-utils` package nor a TypeScript runtime we can assume (the only in-pod `node` is whatever the `claude` CLI ships against, so `--experimental-strip-types` is not safe to rely on), and regex-stripping the type annotations off `command-redaction.ts` would fail silently the first time that file grows syntax the stripper does not know. This follows the repo's own established answer to exactly this problem, twice over: `ENV_GUARD_SCRIPT` carries a second copy of `classifyAgentShellCommand` with one corpus run through both, and `CREDENTIAL_VALUE_RES` is held in parity with `command-redaction.ts` "by a test, not by convention". `pod-log-redactor.test.ts` does **both** halves — structural (every regex literal and hint in `command-redaction.ts` appears in the script, and the rule-name sets are equal, so a NEW rule cannot be silently forgotten) and behavioural over a shared corpus (so a REORDER is caught). The second half is the load-bearing one: this ticket's entire history is rule **order**, not rule presence.

**Every guard has a failing mutation**, one mutation per run, baseline restored between each — and writing them found two guards that were not pinned at all:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| filter moved after `tee` | 1 failed |
| filter removed from the pipeline | 1 failed |
| GitHub rules moved after JWT | 19 failed |
| a rule deleted from the pod script | 1 failed (structural parity) |
| fail-open `=cat` removed | 2 failed |
| **OpenAI rule moved ahead of JWT** | **302 passed — NOT PINNED** |
| **JSON branch removed** | **302 passed — NOT PINNED** |
| no-op redactor (transform emits the raw line) | 1 failed |
| `flush` handler dropped (unterminated tail discarded) | 1 failed |
| `flush` emits the tail UNREDACTED | 1 failed |
| single-var quoting reverted (whitespace `$GUARD_DIR` word-splits) | 1 failed |
| `command -v node` probe dropped | 2 failed |
| `\|\| echo … UNREDACTED` diagnostic dropped | 2 failed |
| braced group returns non-zero (spurious "not installed" next to an installed filter) | 1 failed |

Both gaps are now closed by fixtures that distinguish them, and both re-mutate red. The OpenAI one matters: `COMMAND_OPENAI_KEY_RE` is prefix-anchored and *not* self-sufficient, so ahead of JWT it replaces only `sk-<body>` and strands the dotted tail — leaving `***REDACTED***.c3ludGhldGljLXBheWxvYWQ.c3ludGhldGljLXNpZ25hdHVyZQ`, which is the original 2-of-3-segments leak in the other vendor's shape. Every fixture is synthetic; the ticket's original verifying signal was withdrawn precisely because it required emitting a live credential into the store whose safety was in question.

Each mutation **asserts its own anchor matched exactly once before the suite is read**. That is not ceremony: a substitution that silently fails to apply reports the baseline's green and is indistinguishable from a guard that does not bind. It has already produced one void "5/5 passed" reading on this change — the script lives in a `String.raw` template and the naive `perl` pattern never matched. Two of the rows above were re-anchored for the same reason (`command -v node` also occurs in a docblock, so a `grep` liveness check reported VOID on a mutation that had in fact applied).

**The last three rows are behavioural, and nothing before them was.** Every other assertion about the setup fragment is a *string* match on the generated text, which cannot settle a precedence question: `A && B && { … } || C` fires `C` when **either** probe fails, and would also fire it spuriously if the braced group ever returned non-zero — announcing "not installed" beside a filter that *is* installed. `pod-log-redactor.test.ts` therefore executes the real fragment under `/bin/sh` (the container command is `sh -c`) across all three branches, with `$GUARD_DIR` a tmpdir. Pre-creating the target short-circuits the `[ -f ] ||` install, which is what lets the node-missing case use an empty `PATH` without also breaking `base64` and `mv`.

**Failure posture: fail OPEN, on THREE paths, and say so on two of them.** (1) A throw inside the redactor emits the original line — that is our bug, and both alternatives are worse: dropping the line corrupts the transport *and* the server-side parse. (2) The script is not on disk — a lost install race, an unwritable volume. (3) `node` is not runnable; `[ -f ]` does not cover that, so the fragment probes `command -v node` separately rather than assuming the env-guard established it (that fragment's one node use is explicitly fail-soft). On (2) and (3) `$PAPERCLIP_POD_LOG_FILTER` degrades to `cat`, so neither can fail every run in the fleet through `set -o pipefail`.

Paths (2) and (3) **announce the degradation on stderr**. Silently, "redacted" and "fell open to `cat`" are indistinguishable after the fact — on the one control whose entire purpose is that it held — so a pod log could be read as scrubbed when nothing scrubbed it. Path (1) stays silent by design: it is per-line and inside the script, where a diagnostic would itself be a write into the stream being filtered. The `||` also makes the statement exit 0 rather than leaving a non-zero status mid-fragment.

The install reuses the env-guard's write-once + `mv -f` pattern and a content-addressed filename, because `$GUARD_DIR` is RWX CephFS shared by every agent pod and a wedged truncate there once blocked `open()` fleet-wide.

A case asserts the terminal rate-limit event the awk filter greps for (`"overageStatus":"rejected"` / `"overageDisabledReason":"out_of_credits"`) survives redaction byte-identical, so the RCA 2026-05-06 fail-fast cannot be broken by this.

**This is defence in depth, NOT the durable boundary.** BLO-21027 (remove the credential from the pod at all) is the boundary; nothing here may be relied on to decide who may read a pod log.

**Drive-by, needed to run any of this:** the adapter's `vitest.config.ts` now aliases `@paperclipai/adapter-utils` to the monorepo source. `src/` imports it (`session.ts`, `skills.ts`) and several suites do too, but the package neither declares it nor has a `node_modules` link, so they died at import with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. Measured: master **8 failed suites / 415 passing**; with the alias **3 failed / 863 passing** — 448 tests that were not running at all. The 3 remaining failures are genuinely missing npm packages (`@kubernetes/client-node`, `picocolors`) and are unrelated.
